claim_text: Deep learning segmentation has achieved strong performance across major medical imaging tasks, including multi-organ CT segmentation and MRI lesion segmentation.
notes: Need representative canonical papers rather than exhaustive coverage.

claim_text: In real clinical deployment, closed-set segmentation assumptions are frequently violated by unannotated anatomy, rare pathology, or distribution shift, and silent high-confidence errors can be clinically risky.
notes: Prefer survey or perspective papers covering reliability / uncertainty communication in medical AI.

claim_text: Common ways to handle unknowns after closed-set segmentation include post-hoc risk scores such as MSP, Energy, and MC Dropout variance, as well as auxiliary unknown branches attached to standard segmentation backbones.
notes: Need foundational references for MSP, Energy, MC Dropout, plus representative segmentation-side uncertainty / unknown-branch work.

claim_text: Uncertainty-based unknown handling in medical organ segmentation often produces false positives near anatomical boundaries because partial-volume effects naturally increase uncertainty there.
notes: Prefer medical segmentation papers discussing uncertainty near organ boundaries.

claim_text: Detecting unknown pixels and structuring them into spatially coherent abstention regions are distinct abilities and should not be conflated under a single evaluation lens.
notes: May need adjacent support from selective prediction, open-set segmentation, or reliability framing rather than a direct prior match.

claim_text: Query-based mask parsing and prototype-based decision boundaries provide natural ingredients for building a native unknown-output segmentation framework.
notes: Need representative query-based segmentation and prototype/open-set references.

claim_text: Open-set recognition studies classification with rejection of unseen classes, with representative directions including OpenMax, reciprocal-point learning, placeholder learning, and recent KBS variants for unknown scoring or domain-specific recognition.
notes: Need canonical and recent representative papers, not every sub-variant.

claim_text: Out-of-distribution detection literature includes MSP, Energy, virtual outlier synthesis, vision-language based OoD detection, and broad surveys unifying OoD settings across tasks.
notes: Should include foundational and survey-style references.

claim_text: Open-world object detection extends rejection beyond image-level classification, for example through explicit unknown queries, pseudo-unknown uncertainty learning, or adaptive open-set boundaries.
notes: Need one canonical open-world detector plus the cited KBS-style variants.

claim_text: Medical anomaly and OoD localization benchmarks such as MOOD have encouraged reconstruction-based, self-supervised, and feature-matching approaches for detecting abnormal regions in medical images.
notes: Need MOOD benchmark and representative anomaly segmentation methods.

claim_text: Medical-image uncertainty estimation widely uses MC Dropout, deep ensembles, and evidential formulations, and recent reviews note that evaluation remains mostly pixel-level rather than structure-level.
notes: Need methodological foundations and a review that comments on evaluation granularity.

claim_text: Some medical segmentation work uses uncertainty as an internal training signal or representation-calibration cue, showing that uncertainty can be integrated into the model rather than treated only as post-hoc output.

Selective prediction and abstention allow models to reject low-confidence cases, but dense segmentation raises an additional challenge because abstention must correspond to structured spatial regions rather than whole-image decisions.
notes: Need selective prediction foundations and at least one medical-ML reliability paper if possible.
